title: Severe Hemorrhage Risk (Warfarin + NSAID)
content:
Drug Interaction: Severe Hemorrhage Risk (Warfarin + NSAID)
Primary Drug: warfarin
Interacting Drugs/Classes: nsaid, aspirin, ibuprofen, diclofenac, aceclofenac
Severity: CRITICAL
Clinical Consequence: NSAIDs inhibit platelet aggregation and cause gastric mucosal erosion, dramatically increasing fatal gastrointestinal and intracranial bleeding risk with Warfarin.
Action Required: Avoid concurrent use. Use Paracetamol for analgesia or consult prescribing physician.
action: Avoid concurrent use. Use Paracetamol for analgesia or consult prescribing physician.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Reduced Antiplatelet Efficacy (Clopidogrel + Omeprazole)
content:
Drug Interaction: Reduced Antiplatelet Efficacy (Clopidogrel + Omeprazole)
Primary Drug: clopidogrel
Interacting Drugs/Classes: omeprazole, esomeprazole
Severity: MAJOR
Clinical Consequence: Omeprazole competitively inhibits CYP2C19, preventing conversion of Clopidogrel into its active antiplatelet metabolite. Increases stent thrombosis and re-infarction risk.
Action Required: Switch PPI to Pantoprazole or Rabeprazole (minimal CYP2C19 inhibition).
action: Switch PPI to Pantoprazole or Rabeprazole (minimal CYP2C19 inhibition).
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Potentially Fatal Hypotension (PDE5i + Nitrates)
content:
Drug Interaction: Potentially Fatal Hypotension (PDE5i + Nitrates)
Primary Drug: sildenafil
Interacting Drugs/Classes: nitrates, nitroglycerin, isosorbide dinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate
Severity: CRITICAL
Clinical Consequence: Potentiation of nitric oxide / cGMP pathway causes severe, refractory, life-threatening hypotension and cardiovascular collapse.
Action Required: STRICT ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION. Do not co-administer.
action: STRICT ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION. Do not co-administer.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Severe Hyperkalemia / Dual RAAS Blockade
content:
Drug Interaction: Severe Hyperkalemia / Dual RAAS Blockade
Primary Drug: telmisartan
Interacting Drugs/Classes: spironolactone, potassium chloride, losartan, enalapril, ramipril
Severity: MAJOR
Clinical Consequence: Combining ARBs with ACE inhibitors or potassium-sparing diuretics markedly increases life-threatening hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury, and hypotension.
Action Required: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine. Avoid dual RAAS blockade.
action: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine. Avoid dual RAAS blockade.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Lactic Acidosis Risk (Metformin + Contrast)
content:
Drug Interaction: Lactic Acidosis Risk (Metformin + Contrast)
Primary Drug: metformin
Interacting Drugs/Classes: iodinated contrast, contrast media
Severity: MAJOR
Clinical Consequence: Intravascular iodinated radiocontrast agents can lead to acute renal failure and massive accumulation of metformin, triggering fatal lactic acidosis.
Action Required: Withhold metformin 48 hours prior to and post-contrast imaging.
action: Withhold metformin 48 hours prior to and post-contrast imaging.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Additive QT Prolongation / Torsades de Pointes
content:
Drug Interaction: Additive QT Prolongation / Torsades de Pointes
Primary Drug: azithromycin
Interacting Drugs/Classes: ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, amiodarone, domperidone
Severity: MAJOR
Clinical Consequence: Co-administration of multiple QT-prolonging agents exponentially increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.
Action Required: Avoid combination in patients with underlying cardiac conditions or baseline long QT.
action: Avoid combination in patients with underlying cardiac conditions or baseline long QT.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Serotonin Syndrome & Seizure Threshold Lowering
content:
Drug Interaction: Serotonin Syndrome & Seizure Threshold Lowering
Primary Drug: tramadol
Interacting Drugs/Classes: fluoxetine, sertraline, escitalopram, paroxetine, duloxetine, ssri, snri
Severity: MAJOR
Clinical Consequence: Tramadol inhibits serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake. Concomitant use with SSRIs/SNRIs precipitates potentially fatal Serotonin Syndrome and lowers seizure threshold.
Action Required: Monitor for tremors, hyperreflexia, agitation, and hyperthermia. Reduce tramadol dose.
action: Monitor for tremors, hyperreflexia, agitation, and hyperthermia. Reduce tramadol dose.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix

title: Severe Rhabdomyolysis Risk (Statin + Macrolide/Azole)
content:
Drug Interaction: Severe Rhabdomyolysis Risk (Statin + Macrolide/Azole)
Primary Drug: atorvastatin
Interacting Drugs/Classes: clarithromycin, erythromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole
Severity: MAJOR
Clinical Consequence: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition elevates atorvastatin serum concentrations by up to 400%, precipitating severe myopathy, acute rhabdomyolysis, and renal failure.
Action Required: Temporarily suspend statin therapy during course of antibiotic/antifungal.
action: Temporarily suspend statin therapy during course of antibiotic/antifungal.
source: FDA/BNF Pharmacological Matrix
